## 15 November: Warsaw radio personnel and a repeated key notice

<a id="november-15-warsaw-radio-personnel-and-a-repeated-key-notice"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p197 A1, p197 A2, p197 B.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov15-radio-personnel-and-key-notice-november-15-warsaw-radio-personnel-and-a-repeated-key-notice"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p197 preserves a two-part order concerning radio personnel in Warsaw
and a second physical witness of the [p189 C December-key notice](189.md#edition-cases-context-p189-c).
All three records use the unchanged published **Nov13–15b** key. The first
part of the personnel order has a five-slot source deficit; its proposed
reconstruction is explicitly conditional. The complete second part directly
names **Posen** and reads **`IN MARSCH ZU SETZEN`**.

| Record | Printed source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Inserted-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p197 A1 | 193 | 198, conditional gap | 93/99 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| p197 A2 | 144 | 144, native | 68/72 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| p197 B | 124 | 124, native | 60/62 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

The counts describe the stated frames and proposals, including unresolved
numerical labels. They do not count every displayed label as an independently
authenticated historical character. Period-key credit remains with George
Lasry and collaborators as recorded in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).


**Reviewed source crops:** [p197_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/sources/p197_reviewed.png) · [p189_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/sources/p189_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

### p197 A1

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — shared header and first-part length:**

```text
A) WAU v LP (03.55 p.m., November 15th)
14.50 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-198
```

</details>

The five printed rows contain **193 slots**, including one dash in `VDVG-`,
against the advertised **198**. This edition keeps those 193 source slots
unchanged in the literal record. Its proposed analysis frame inserts **five
unknown slots at source boundary 165**, between the final row's `AFXFF` and
`GFVAX`. That location is an editorial hypothesis, not a printed gap mark.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 198-slot frame with five added unknown slots; 93/99 fixed positions:**

```text
FESTUNGSFUNKAXWARSCHAUXDASGESAMTE?MBEREIC?DESGOUV?RNEMENT?WARSCHA?VERFUEGBAREFUN?ERPERSONALISTNMCHX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; one observed-coordinate substitution, one source-mask fill and five inserted-slot fills; 99/99 fixed positions:**

```text
FESTUNGSFUNKAXWARSCHAUXDASGESAMTEIMBEREICHDESGOUVERNEMENTSWARSCHAUVERFUEGBAREFUNKERPERSONALISTNACHX
```

</details>

The complete price, with zero-based source indices, is:

| Operation | Location | Proposed value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | Source index 98 | `A → V`, giving `NACH` in place of raw `NMCH` |
| Source-mask fill | Printed dash at source index 134 | `D` |
| Five-slot insertion and fills | Source boundary 165 | `AAFFX` |

**Readable German — complete edited stream under the conditional gap model:**

> Festungsfunka Warschau. Das gesamte im Bereich des Gouvernements Warschau verfuegbare Funkerpersonal ist nach

`FESTUNGSFUNKA` is retained as transmitted. The sentence continues in the
native second part. That continuation independently gives the destination
and action, but does not supply every missing first-part letter.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov15-radio-personnel-and-key-notice-comparison-of-the-possible-gap-locations"></a>

#### Comparison of the possible gap locations

For this exact 99-position candidate and the unchanged key, the verifier
compares **all 194 source boundaries** at which one five-coordinate gap
could be inserted. It prices only changes to observed coordinates in the
following column; the one printed-mask fill and five added-slot fills remain
separate in every comparison.

| Source boundary | Observed-coordinate substitutions |
| ---: | ---: |
| 163 | 2 |
| 164 | 2 |
| **165** | **1** |
| 166 | 2 |
| Every other boundary | At least 3 |

Boundary 165 is the unique minimum **for this candidate and this single-gap
family**. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/certificates.json)
retains all prices and the raw domains and edits for every frame within one
substitution of the minimum. The comparison does not prove unique historical
wording or exclude other damage mechanisms. The untouched 193-slot decode
and its unpaired final coordinate are retained separately in the certificate.

<a id="source-p197-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov15-radio-personnel-and-key-notice-p197-a2"></a>

### p197 A2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — second-part label:**

```text
2 TL RICHI-144
```

**Raw output — native 144-slot frame; 68/72 fixed positions:**

```text
XFESTUNGSFUNKAXPOSENXINMARSCHZUSETZENXXINACHXFUNKLEITUNGHEIMATXNRX???6?5
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Festungsfunka Posen in Marsch zu setzen. I Nach Funkleitung Heimat Nr ???6?5.

No coordinate or key change is used. The literal sequence **`INACH`** is
shown as **`I Nach`**, without expanding it into an office or correcting it
into a different signature. The source's `VD AVD` is five printed
coordinates despite its internal space.

The final **`???6?5`** remains six output positions. The first, second and
fifth labels arise from three different unknown square cells; the second
and third positions use the **same** cell and must have the same value.
Each unknown cell has domain `{2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, Q, Y}` under the published
partial square, and different cells must remain distinct. This coupled
uncertainty is retained in the certificate; no historical reference number
is assigned.

Under the separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md),
the first reference digit becomes **2**, giving `2??6?5` and **69/72**
fixed positions. The repeated middle cell and the fifth label remain
unresolved; no coordinate change is needed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov15-radio-personnel-and-key-notice-p197-b"></a>

### p197 B

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (04.24 p.m., November 15th)
10.00 (15/11)
RIZI-124-
```

</details>

The dash after the length label is outside the ciphertext. The visible
final group `XFXX` belongs to the 124-slot body; the earlier OCR omitted it.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 124-slot frame; 60/62 fixed positions:**

```text
UNLOES?A?EHUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions; no fills; 62/62 fixed positions:**

```text
UNLOESBAREFUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

</details>

The changes are **source index 23 V→F**, **62 A→D**, and **93 F→G**. Unknown
square cells are not filled to make these words: the letters B and R already
occupy other cells, so the corresponding word proposals require coordinate
changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Unloesbare Funksprueche nach Dezemberschluessel entziffern. Irrtum.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov15-radio-personnel-and-key-notice-what-the-second-copy-supports"></a>

#### Letter support from the second copy

The independently inspected [p189 C source — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/inputs.json)
has the same 124-coordinate body except **source index 93**, where p189
prints **G** and p197 prints **F**. Their reception times differ; the common
internal `10.00` and 15 November date are preserved.

That single difference accounts for **B** versus an unknown at plaintext
index **6**. Thus p189's raw reading directly supports the proposed B in
p197. Both copies still have the unknown at plaintext index **8** and raw H
at index **10**. Neither copy independently supplies the proposed R or F at
those two positions. Their shared repairs are not promoted into independent
corroboration.

**`DEZEMBER`** and **`IRRTUM`** are directly decoded in both copies. The final
word is retained without deciding whether it corrects, cancels or otherwise
qualifies the preceding instruction.

## Equipment and lorry orders — p197/p198 parallels

**Sources on this page:** p197 C, p197 D.

**Related source pages:** [p198 B](198.md#source-p198-b), [p198 E](198.md#source-p198-e).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-equipment-and-lorry-orders--p197p198-parallels"></a>


[Earlier transport traffic](#edition-cases-context-transport)

**Source linkage, reconstruction and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
Four additional intercepts extend the transport conversation under the
previously published 13 November–15b key. They concern equipment for Darmstadt
and a lorry, trailer and petrol pump. Their source disagreements and length
repairs remain explicit. The separate [p198 D challenge](198.md#edition-cases-p198) is still open.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-most-likely-readings"></a>

### Most likely readings

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-equipment-for-darmstadt--p197-c--p198-b"></a>

#### Equipment for Darmstadt — p197 C / p198 B

**Readable German:**

> Nachr.-Chef. [EINHAFEN: unclear designation]. Zwei US-Geraete nach Darmstadt
> verladen. Station bleibt bis [16X0???] betr.-bereit. Seifert.

**Meaning:** Chief of signals; an unidentified designation follows. Load two
`US` apparatuses for Darmstadt. Keep the station operational until an unresolved
date/time. Signed Seifert. The abbreviations are read as *Nachrichtenchef* and
*betriebsbereit*; their full spellings were not transmitted.

The source-supported editorial template is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXEINHAFENXZWEIUSGERAETENACHDARMSTADTVERLADENX
STATIONBLEIBTBIS16X0???BETRBEREITXSEIFERT
```

</details>

Of its **92 specified characters out of 95**, 91 have a complete coordinate
pair in at least one aligned witness. The `E` in `VERLADEN` additionally needs
an erasure fill. Across both witnesses that choice also requires one known
coordinate change above the attainable minimum: **19 changes rather than 18**.
This is an edited composite of conflicting copies, not a clean full reading
already present in either copy.

**Terminology:** `US` plausibly refers to contemporary radio apparatus using
undamped waves. The manufacturer's *Telefunken-Zeitung*, no. 15 (May 1919),
shows an apparatus labelled `Tragbares U S Gerät 17` on printed page 15 and
records delivery of a `U-S-Gerät` on page 16, beside its discussion of
undamped-wave equipment. This supports the equipment interpretation; it does
not identify the specific model in the telegram. See the
[primary journal](https://www.radiomuseum.org/forumdata/users/5100/TZ_3Jg_Nr15_1v1_v10.pdf#page=16)
and [terminology review](../../data/reviews/transport_terminology.json).

`EINHAFEN` is retained without a place identification. The date/time is not
silently normalized to 16:00: the witnesses actually disagree in its final
positions.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-lorry-trailer-and-petrol-pump--p197-d--p198-e"></a>

#### Lorry, trailer and petrol pump — p197 D / p198 E

**Readable German:**

> Es kommt ein [?]-Tonnen-Auto. Nur besten [Anhaenger] beladen.
> [Benzinpumpe] bereithalten.

**Meaning:** A lorry of unresolved tonnage is coming. Load only the best
trailer and have the petrol pump ready. The bracketed words include explicit
editorial changes; the tonnage is not a recovered digit.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ESKOMMTEIN?TONNENAUTOXNURBESTENANHAENGERBELADENX
BENZINPUMPEBEREITHALTEN
```

</details>

Of **70 specified characters out of 71**, 66 have a complete observed pair,
one combines coordinate halves from the two witnesses, and three require
unattested coordinate changes. The preferred wording costs **13** known
coordinate changes across the two copies; their attainable minimum is **8**.
The extra changes affect `A`, `E` in `ANHAENGER` and `Z` in `BENZIN`.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-linked-number-fields"></a>

### Linked number fields

The shared partial square links several unresolved characters across the
conversation. These identities help future recovery without choosing a digit:

| Field | Shared square cell |
| --- | --- |
| Lorry tonnage in p197 D / p198 E | `FV` |
| Hour digit in the planned `1?00` departure, p194 A / p196 B | `FV` |
| Hour digit in the reported `1?00` departure, p197 E / p198 C | `AF` |
| Hour digit in the apparent readiness time `0?05`, p197 C | `GA` |
| Men remaining, p197 E / p198 C | `GD` |

The planned and reported hour digits therefore **differ** under the common
bijective square. The tonnage equals the planned-hour digit. Under the
published partial key, treating all four distinct fields as ordinary
decimal digits gives **360** assignments. A same-day departure no later
than the `13.45` origin field could then be 12:00 or 13:00. Further assuming
the same movement and prohibiting early departure gave the earlier scenario
“planned 12:00, departed 13:00, a 2-ton lorry.”

The [shared conditional VG=2 interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
changes that comparison. Digit 2 belongs to VG and cannot also occupy
either hour cell. The four decimal fields now have **120** assignments.
If the reported departure is same-day and before `13.45`, it must be
**13:00**, assigning **AF=3**; **24** joint field assignments remain. The
planned-hour/tonnage cell FV is then one of `4, 7, 8, 9`.

No assignment satisfies the additional “no early departure” condition.
The earlier 12:00/13:00 scenario and the new award-class interpretation are
therefore incompatible within this square. Neither the common-movement
assumption nor the chronology is supplied by the ciphertext. The current
readings retain the unknown time fields, with the 13:00 branch recorded
separately in the [joint transport certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/transport_certificate.json).
The p198 C source itself prints a `13.03 p.m.` receipt before its `13.45`
origin time, so the recorded times cannot all be accepted without qualification.

The [linked-field analysis](../../experiments/transport_followup/linked_fields.json)
records the exact source indices and the earlier three scenario counts; its separate
enumeration checks every one of the square's 40,320 bijective completions.
An [independent review](../../data/reviews/transport_linked_fields_independent.json)
reconstructs the mappings by column offsets and confirms that every tied
source geometry gives the same field identities.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-what-was-repaired"></a>

### Source defects and reconstruction models

| Source | Literal evidence | Stated reconstruction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p197 C | 185 slots against a `RIZI-190` label; six dashes and an invalid `C` | Insert five unknown coordinates. All 186 boundaries were checked; positions 64 and 65 tie and yield the same masked stream. |
| p198 B | 190 valid coordinates | Kept as printed; its disagreements with the proposed reading are recorded separately. |
| p197 D | 142 slots, including one dash at position 89 | A conditional relocation of that dash preserves the order of every known coordinate. Positions 74 and 75 tie among all 142 placements; both survive. |
| p198 E | 147 slots against a `RIZI-142` label; adjacent `XAXVV XAXVV` and an invalid `K` | Delete either identical five-coordinate group. Both deletions give the same 142-slot stream, preserving 141 valid coordinates. |

All positions above are zero-based. Minimum disagreement is an alignment
criterion; it does not establish that a proposed loss or misplaced dash
actually occurred. The two raw source readings, every tied geometry, and all
per-letter alternatives are available in the
[full experiment](../../experiments/transport_followup/README.md).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport"></a>

## p197 E — Lorry departure and men remaining until Sunday

**Edition context:** Transport traffic — p185/p189 and parallel messages.

**Related source pages:** [p185 D](185.md#source-p185-d), [p189 E](189.md#source-p189-e), [p193 E](193.md#source-p193-e), [p194 A](194.md#source-p194-a), [p196 B](196.md#source-p196-b), [p198 C](198.md#source-p198-c).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-transport-traffic--p185p189-and-parallel-messages"></a>



**Status: source-preserving partial reading under a plausible, unproved gap geometry.** This supplementary **p185 D** intercept is outside the 22-message challenge. Its header reads `CM v CZ (20.15 p.m., November 13th), 21.00, RIZI-198`, but the body contains 193 slots: 192 valid ADFGVX coordinates and one literal `Y`. The raw `Y` is retained in the source layer and treated as one unknown coordinate in analysis.

**Current transcription, comparison and verification:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Historical keys and source witnesses retain the provenance recorded in the certificate.

<a id="source-p197-e"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-independent-transport-context"></a>

### Independent transport context

Six additional source-checked intercepts decrypt directly with the same historical key. They retain every literal garble and unresolved square cell:

- **p193 E, 14 November:** `KLEINERFEDERWAGENZU?ANHAENGENHIERXKOMMTAUTOX`
- **p194 A, 14 November, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITCGDHFN1?00XWAGENBERE?THALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT`
- **p196 B, 15 November, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEI?ERT`
- **p197 E, 15 November, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00A?GEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSOHNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSE?FERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p198 C, 15 November, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00ABGEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSONNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSEHFERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p189 E, 15 November, header `CZ v CM`:** `JAHEBEPUMPEAUSBLECHXKOMMEN?AUTOSXHIER?ANH?ENGER`. This is a different intercept from the p189 challenge target.

The p194/p196 pair repeats `DHFN` and names `HANAU` as the march destination. It has 171 of 174 raw coordinates in common; disagreements are at indices 82 (`K/X`), 167 (`X/V`), and 173 (`D/G`). The p197/p198 pair agrees at 183 of 186 coordinates, differing at indices 59 (`V/A`), 63 (`A/V`), and 67 (`G/A`). Neither lorry-message copy supplies an exact `SEIFERT` signature; `SEHFERT` is not silently corrected.

For the transport-order pair, a separately labelled source-supported composite takes `X` at index 82 and `V` at index 167 from p196 while retaining p194's `D` at index 173. It reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional source-supported composite of the p194 and p196 witnesses:**

```text
ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT
```

</details>

This composite fixes 86 of 87 characters. It makes an editorial choice
between disagreeing source witnesses, with every chosen value attested in
at least one. The certificate retains all four combinations of the two
disagreements between valid coordinates. The planned-time cell `FV`
remains unassigned.

Under the separate shared VG=2 interpretation, the reported-hour cell
`AF` cannot also be 2. If the departure occurred on the report's date
before its `13.45` origin time, `1?00` therefore becomes **13:00**. That
chronological assumption is kept separate from the source-supported
composite. The [linked-field comparison](#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-linked-number-fields)
also shows why this reading cannot be combined with the earlier extra
assumption that the reported departure was no earlier than the planned one.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p185_D_transport.json) contains every gap geometry, its full plaintext domains, exact source-to-plaintext mapping, all six direct context readings, both near-parallel comparisons, and the conditional composite. The [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/transport.py) recomputes all 194 constraint sets and exact coordinate roundtrips without a language model. It checks the consistency of the stored ranking order but does not recompute the heuristic scores. The [portable ranking script](../../experiments/known_key/README.md) reproduces both complete rankings from a pinned upstream model; every stored score matched exactly in the recorded environment.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.transport
```

This analysis does not fully solve p189 and does not add a solved item to the 22-message total.

Four [additional p197/p198 witnesses](#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198) now connect the
conversation with equipment for Darmstadt, a lorry, a trailer and a petrol
pump. Their duplicate-group and missing-coordinate hypotheses have separate
source and arithmetic certificates.

Source images: [p189](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_context.png), [p193](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p193_context.png), [p194](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p194_context.png), [p196](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p196_context.png), [p197](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p197_context.png), [p198](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p198_context.png). ### Most likely readings

| Record | Readable German text | Meaning and uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p185 D, conditional word completion | […] marschiert Lastautos morgen 1500 ueber DHFN. Abmarschbereit sein. […] Seifert. | The reconstructed clause concerns trucks moving tomorrow via `DHFN` and orders readiness to depart. Three coordinate substitutions and three fills complete the words; the opening and closing instruction remain damaged. |

Seifert. | Departure as arranged on Friday; keep vehicles ready; Hanau is the destination. Every selected coordinate is attested in one of the two witnesses, but one time digit remains unknown. |
| p197 E / p198 C | Lastauto 1?00 abgefahren. Ich bleibe mit ? Mann bis Sonntag. Alles Gute, auf Wiedersehen. [Seifert]. Gruss Bocho. | The truck has departed; the sender remains with an unknown number of men until Sunday. The signature is normalized editorially; neither witness spells it exactly this way. |

Brackets mark editorial interpretations; `?` retains an unresolved character. `DHFN`, `STATMET` and `BOCHO` are not expanded or geographically identified. The exact readings and witness disagreements follow below.
